doc.title: Phil Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 27, 2023

title: Learning arranging by ear; working out Hank Jones's chord
summary: Wilson and Rowe compare self-taught arranging; he spent two weeks working out a chord from a Jazz at the Philharmonic record.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Let me ask you some more about that. I may be a bit like you with arranging.
Yeah. I never had books, I mostly absorbed what I was hearing from big bands and —
And tried to make it, you know I would sit at the piano and say well if the saxes are doing this then maybe the trombones could do that and trial and error.

Can I — I’ve got to tell you, this is a true story now. When we were in Exeter in this big dorm that my dad — my room was on the third floor of our apartment and the piano was on the first floor. And I’m listening to Jazz at the Philharmonic Volume 9 or 10, and in it Hank Jones is playing the piano and Bill Harris is playing the trombone and Dizzy you know and it’s a ten inch you know. And in the middle of I think it was Bill Harris’s solo Hank Jones hits a D/C7, in other words the upper structure triad, right? And I said, “Oh man.” I mean he hits it and then moves on in the bridge of “Perdido” I think it was, right?

And I said oh I love the sound of that chord. I wanted to know what that chord was. So I ran down two flights of stairs to the piano and started — I wish I had a piano here to demonstrate because it was funny. No. No. No. No. So I’d run up two flights of stairs and put it on, a 78 you know — it was not a — no that was an LP a 10 inch. And so finally this went on for over two weeks, up and down. I’m going to find that mother you know. And so finally — oh no, I took a red pencil and when it hit on the LP the C7 sharp 11 I marked it with red you know so I could just drop the needle on it. I did get it after two weeks. I told Hank Jones that years later when he was at some festival. He got a good laugh out of it.
That is some paying of dues right there.
